ABI.input_data: Pointer to constant-buffer bytes, not userdata; documented input. Copy dataSize bytes into retained allocation while callback is active; do not retain the incoming CPU pointer or mutate it.
ABI.dataSize: 64-bit byte count by value. Local backend passes num32BitEntries*sizeof(uint32_t). No maximum, size-return field or recoverable callback failure protocol is specified in these public declarations.
ABI.return_by_value: FfxApiConstantBufferAllocation contains FfxApiResource resource and uint64_t handle.
ABI.resource: Public declaration describes the constant-buffer resource. Local DX12 consumer ignores allocation.resource; fallback explicitly returns an empty resource with comment Not needed for directx. This source behavior is not a guarantee about a different private signed provider.
ABI.handle: Local source casts handle to D3D12_GPU_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS and calls SetComputeRootConstantBufferView. It is an address in this DX12 path, not an SRV descriptor heap handle or CPU pointer.
ABI.size_alignment: Reserve at least dataSize bytes, conservatively round each extent/offset to256 bytes. Local fallback does this; pinned Windows SDK D3D12_CONSTANT_BUFFER_DATA_PLACEMENT_ALIGNMENT is256. RootCBV binding carries address only, no SizeInBytes descriptor.
ABI.calling_convention: Callback typedef has no extra calling-convention or userdata annotation. Future code must match the exact SDK typedef and target x64 compiler ABI; no callback adapter or layout experiment was compiled here.

registration.other_callback_fields: Resource/heap allocator+deallocator pointers may remain null. Custom CB field can be nonnull by itself in checked-in CreateBackend source.
registration.CPU_memCb: ffxAllocationCallbacks memCb has separate pUserData/alloc/dealloc; it is host-memory allocation, not the CB callback userdata. Current FSRD calls CreateContext with NULL memCb.
registration.source_scope: Local source s_fpConstantAllocator is module-static, not stored per BackendContext. Setter assigns global pointer without a lock. CreateBackend registers only nonnull; null descriptor does not clear earlier registration. Destruction code does not reset that pointer.
registration.documented_scope: Five public headers do not specify per-context isolation, concurrent registration, callback thread, synchronous-only invocation, release notification, AddRef/ownership transfer, or post-Dispatch callback quiescence.
registration.timing_source_bound: Checked-in executeGpuJobCompute invokes allocator inline before rootCBV binding. This shows local function call order only; it does not prove private signed-provider call timing or thread behavior.

source_default.upload_resource: Lazy committed UPLOAD buffer in GENERIC_READ, persistently mapped.
source_default.allocation: Mutex guards CPU buffer/offset/memcpy. Each allocation rounds up256, wraps when offset+size>=capacity, returns GPUVA+offset.
source_default.capacity: Local FFX_BUFFER_SIZE4096 *maxEffectContexts *FFX_MAX_PASS_COUNT50 *FFX_MAX_QUEUED_FRAMES4 =819200 bytes per maxEffectContext. This is checked-in source configuration, not measured provider allocation capacity or proof that K4 always fits.
source_default.limitations: Mutex is CPU mutual exclusion. Fallback itself has no fence check before wrap. CPU staging ring and private SRV/UAV descriptor rings are separate; custom CB allocator does not replace them or repair bytes already overwritten before callback.

production.actual_chain: FSRD context -> ffxCreateBackendDX12Desc(device) -> ffxOverrideVersion. No allocation-callback descriptor. D3D12_CreateContext routes denoiser context into loaded denoiser module.
production.qualification: No repository production path explicitly registers/uses callback. This cannot exclude another host component or a private provider installing one internally.

future_diagnostic_feasibility.answer: Yes at the declared extension surface, conditionally: an isolated future child could return fresh immutable GPU-visible constant storage per callback, leaving ordinary7guides, dispatch controls and SDK private descriptor storage untouched.
future_diagnostic_feasibility.preservation: Only add CB allocation descriptor; retain exact provider, flags, guides, queued source frames, constants and batching. No resource/heap callbacks or private SRV edits.
future_diagnostic_feasibility.lifecycle: Retain arena resources, bytes, callback code/state and conservative create-descriptor chain from before CreateContext through all relevant GPU fence completion and context destruction; keep callback state through provider unload/process exit. No returned allocation reuse within the diagnostic. Callbacks and record writes need allocator-level synchronization independent of caller thread.
future_diagnostic_feasibility.process_isolation: Fresh process per default/custom arm and one device/context per process avoids module-static sticky registration and lack of userdata context routing. Do not rely on TLS or stack current-context state to classify callbacks.
future_diagnostic_feasibility.bounded_readiness: Record actual invocation count, thread IDs, dataSize, incoming-byte digest, GPUVA/resource/offset/range, immutable-memory digest and final completion fences. Verify nonoverlap and callback use. The ABI supplies no recoverable OOM result; exhaustion/failure behavior must be explicitly resolved before future execution, not represented by invented valid GPUVA.
future_diagnostic_feasibility.source_vs_binary: Header recognition and actual invocation by the pinned signed provider remain empirical readiness items; local backend source is not proof of binary equivalence.

interpretation.if_batch_difference_disappears: With verified callback use, immutable nonoverlapping bytes/addresses and otherwise matched arms, evidence supports an allocation-path-dependent contribution to the tested batch sensitivity. It does not prove default CB wrap as sole cause: GPUVA/resource layout, timing, memory pressure and opaque scheduling also change.
interpretation.if_difference_persists: Shows that freezing these returned CB allocations alone did not remove the tested effect. Does not exonerate upstream staged constants, uncovered/private constant paths, SDK CPU/history advancement, private descriptor/SRV reuse or other state.
interpretation.if_callback_not_invoked: No allocator contrast was established; zero invocations are not evidence that custom allocation fixes or excludes anything.
not_established: No observed game submission depth, stain/wave cause, quality acceptance, universal SDK bug, safe production fix or private-SRV correctness.
All64 successful SDK recordings/queued executions in batching preserve CPU API advancement; custom allocation still does not separate every opaque provider mechanism.

No public callback threading/sync, per-context routing, AddRef/release or callback error contract was found in pinned5headers.
No assumption that private callbacks are synchronous or asynchronous; design retains state and synchronizes independently.
